title: One answer the text settles
statement: A choice question needs one answer the text settles; check the right option, and each wrong one, on its own.

the answer key itself must be both **complete** (every option that is correct under the stem is keyed) and **exclusive** (no keyed option is actually incorrect). A correct option left out of the key, or an incorrect option included in the key, mismeasures every student and is a factual error in the item — not a stylistic preference. Do NOT excuse a missing-correct option by arguing the keyed options are "the best" ones; "select all that apply" means all.

A hot text item must have exactly the keyed set as its defensible answer. "It is the best span" does NOT rescue the item when another selectable span also satisfies the literal instruction — ambiguous keys mismeasure students.
